comparison: Both evaluate claims C1 and C2 regarding MAP6-CRMP interactions. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns about using MAP6-N isoform antibodies when subicular neurons express MAP6-E isoform, and missing input controls for pulldown assays.

Both address CRMP4 specificity via siRNA knockdown (C3-C6). OpenEval finds claims C3-C9 SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical significance and controls. Peer reviewers rate C3-C6 as UNCERTAIN, requesting quantification of knockdown extent to properly interpret CRMP4 specificity versus incomplete CRMP1/CRMP2 knockdown.

OpenEval evaluates C3-C9 together as SUPPORTED, including genetic knockout data (C7-C8) and rescue experiments (C9). Peer reviewers separately evaluate C7-C9 as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional primary culture measurements from CRMP4-KO neurons to complement siRNA experiments, suggesting current evidence is insufficient.

Both evaluate claims C10 and C11 regarding CRMP4 expression patterns. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting discrepancies between diffuse in vivo staining and enriched neurite localization in primary culture, requesting verification of staining specificity.

Both address anatomical measurements of fornix defects. OpenEval finds C12-C15 SUPPORTED with quantitative data and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate C12-C17 as UNCERTAIN, requesting investigation of underlying causes (neuron specification, mistargeting vs. growth failure) and questioning the characterization as 'developmental delay,' indicating incomplete phenotypic analysis.

OpenEval evaluates C16-C18 as SUPPORTED, noting persistence of defects and appropriate neuron counts ruling out cell loss. Peer reviewers partially overlap (C16-C17) but request more complete phenotypic characterization including analysis of fiber targeting and growth, as done in prior Sema3E knockout work.

OpenEval includes C18 (neuron counts) in broader evaluation of developmental defect persistence (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers separately acknowledge C18 as SUPPORTED, addressing one aspect of their concern about neuron specification and maintenance, though embedded in broader requests for phenotypic analysis.

Both evaluate genetic interaction between CRMP4 and Sema3E (C19, C20, C44). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate breeding strategy and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, describing the genetic interaction data as 'generally of high quality' with no specific concerns raised.

Both address CRMP4 interactions with receptor components (C21-C23). OpenEval finds the co-immunoprecipitation data SUPPORTED with reasonable inferences. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting investigation of ligand-dependence of interactions and noting unconvincing western blots with high background in control conditions.

Both evaluate DRM localization claims (C24-C28). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate markers and quantitative analysis. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, specifically criticizing western blot quality with excessive background pulldown in CRMP4-absent conditions, challenging the biochemical evidence quality.

Both address functional requirement for DRM domains (C29-C30). OpenEval finds the MβCD disruption data SUPPORTED with appropriate dose-response and statistics. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, accepting the functional requirement despite requesting better quantification of other biochemical data.

Both evaluate signaling pathway analysis (C31-C37). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED despite noting some variability. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting quantification, statistical comparison, noting subtle effects, questioning which GSK3 isoform is phosphorylated, and identifying missing loading controls.

Both evaluate phosphorylation mutant rescue experiments (C38-C40). OpenEval rates it UNCERTAIN, acknowledging unexpected findings and unclear interpretation requiring additional experiments. Peer reviewers also rate it UNCERTAIN, requesting verification that mutant proteins are comparably expressed and more detailed methodological descriptions of electroporation procedures.

Both address main conclusions (C41-C43, C45, C87-C88). OpenEval finds conclusions SUPPORTED by collective evidence. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting that while data generally support major conclusions and are of high quality, multiple specific concerns about quantification, controls, and data completeness need addressing before full validation.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic model claims (C62-C67) as SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer reviewers include these claims in their broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of main conclusions (R13), requiring better substantiation of data analysis, interpretation, and quantification before accepting the mechanistic model.

Both evaluate comparison to Sema3E-KO phenotype (C91). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED based on anatomical phenotype similarities. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting incomplete description of prior Sema3E work, requesting more thorough documentation and analysis of underlying causes, and questioning the 'developmental delay' characterization.

OpenEval evaluates C89 (positive control) as SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance. Peer reviewers include C89 in their evaluation of siRNA knockdown experiments (R2), requesting quantification of knockdown extent but not specifically challenging the positive control result.

OpenEval evaluates C92 (speculation about behavioral phenotypes) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is explicitly speculative without behavioral data in the manuscript. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific speculative claim.

OpenEval evaluates C93 (interpretation of DRM function in receptor clustering) as SUPPORTED by experimental findings and consistent with established models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this interpretive conclusion.

OpenEval evaluates C94-C96 (speculative explanations for phosphorylation mutant rescue) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but untested hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these speculative mechanistic explanations.
